zones.what: Lifeboats mounted at Deck 1 obstruct views from Decks 1, 2, and 6, with Deck 1 having the most severe obstruction and Deck 6 having partial obstruction where the horizon remains visible above the boat line.
zones.effect: Ocean view cabins see lifeboats instead of open water when looking down or straight out; the horizon and sky remain clear above, so sunset and sea gazing work but the full seascape is interrupted.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to first-time cruisers or those expecting unobstructed ocean views; experienced cruisers and those focused on value over view typically accept this trade-off, especially on lower decks where rates are better.

zones.what: Lido Deck pool area, buffet, and outdoor activity zones sit directly above on Deck 11 and the upper superstructure.
zones.effect: Daytime noise from pool deck furniture, music, and foot traffic; early morning buffet setup noise; potential for water splashing or drainage sounds during pool operations.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and those valuing quiet mornings should avoid; party-seekers and those out all day won't notice.

zones.what: Main dining rooms and galley operations on Deck 2 and Deck 1 sit two to six decks below these mid-to-aft cabins.
zones.effect: Generally well-insulated by distance; galley noise and vibration rarely penetrate this far up, though occasional late-night service elevator activity may be audible in cabins near vertical service cores.
zones.mattersTo: Low concern for most guests; only hyper-sensitive sleepers in cabins immediately above service areas might notice.

zones.what: Main theatre (Spectacular!) sits on Decks 2-5 forward; show times and lobby activity create noise events directly below these forward cabins.
zones.effect: Bass from sound system and audience applause during evening shows (typically 7pm and 9:30pm); lobby crowd noise before and after performances.
zones.mattersTo: Early-to-bed guests and families with young children should avoid forward on these decks; night owls and show-goers won't be in the cabin during these hours anyway.

zones.what: Primary elevator banks run through midship sections with machinery and waiting areas creating consistent service cores.
zones.effect: Cabins within two or three doors of elevators get frequent ding/door sounds and hallway conversation at all hours; offset by maximum convenience for embark/debark, dining, and deck access.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests and those prioritizing convenience should seek these; light sleepers should stay at least four cabin numbers away from elevator lobbies.

zones.what: Propulsion machinery sits low and aft; these cabins are closest to engine room bulkheads and propeller shafts.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and hum, most noticeable during maneuvering, rough seas, or high-speed transits; modern dampening reduces this but doesn't eliminate it.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive guests and those bothered by constant background hum should avoid; guests seeking value pricing and those who sleep through anything won't mind.

zones.what: Bow thrusters operate during docking and maneuvering in port; anchor chain and windlass sit at the very bow on these lower forward decks.
zones.effect: Thruster rumble during port arrival and departure (brief but intense); anchor chain roar during early morning port arrivals as chain pays out through the hawsepipe.
zones.mattersTo: The 6am anchor drop will wake everyone in forward cabins on port days; only deep sleepers or those already planning to wake early should book the lowest forward sections.

zones.what: Main crew corridor (I-95) runs the length of these lower decks with service access points near midship and aft elevator lobbies.
zones.effect: Crew foot traffic, equipment movement, and service door activity during night turndown and early morning cabin steward rounds; brief but frequent interruptions.
zones.mattersTo: Cabins near crew doors (typically marked on deck plans) may hear door closures and brief conversations during service hours; most guests sleep through it, but light sleepers should check proximity to crew access.
